Empirical Research Plan: “Insider Trading in CDS Prior to Major Credit Events”

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Strategy: Event-time difference-in-differences (DiD) / event-study that compares (i) CDS-spread changes for firms that will soon experience a credit event (“event firms”) in the K days before the public announcement to (ii) the same firms outside that window and/or matched non-event firms during the same calendar days.  We then interact the pre-event indicators with the size of the firm’s lending syndicate to test whether abnormal pre-event activity is stronger when more potential insiders exist (“difference-in-difference-in-differences”, DDD).

Why appropriate:
• Timing of credit events is exogenous to the daily movement of CDS quotes in the immediate past.  
• We observe the entire time-series of CDS spreads for the same entity, so we can absorb permanent differences with entity fixed effects and calendar-date fixed effects to control for market-wide shocks.  
• Parallel-trend assumption is testable with placebo leads (e.g., −90 to −30 days) and with matched non-event firms.  
• The interaction with syndicate size provides cross-sectional variation in private-information intensity, sharpening identification.

Formally:  

Δlog(CDS)i,t = Στ≠0 βτ·Leadτ,it + Στ≠0 γτ·(Leadτ,it × HighLendersi)  
                  + θXi,t + αi + δt + εi,t  

where Leadτ = 1 if day t is τ days relative to the event date (τ<0 pre-event, τ>0 post), HighLenders = 1 if DealScan reports syndicate size above median, Xi,t are controls (equity return, VIX, industry CDS index).

βτ captures average abnormal CDS changes for event firms relative to their own far-from-event days and relative to all other firms on the same calendar day (δt).  γτ is the incremental effect attributable to many potential insiders.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable(s)
• EventWindowit: indicators for each pre-event lead (e.g., −1 to −5, −6 to −10, −11 to −20 trading days).
• HighLendersi: 1 if number of lenders ≥ sample median (or log(#lenders) as continuous).

Control groups / counterfactuals
A. Within-firm, outside the lead window (τ < −60 or τ > +60).  
B. Other firms (no event in ±60 days) on the same calendar date.  
C. Low-lender event firms act as an additional control for the High × Lead interaction.

Treatment timing
Event date 0 = first public announcement of downgrade, default, or LBO.  Leads τ<0 are “treatment” periods where inside information could be exploited.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A1. Parallel trends.  Conditional on controls and fixed effects, CDS spreads of event firms would have moved like those of control firms in the absence of the event until the public announcement.  
 Plausibility: Many macro and sector shocks are absorbed by δt and industry CDS index; testable using placebo leads.

A2. No other simultaneous firm-specific news in the lead window that is both (i) public and (ii) correlated with syndicate size.  
 Plausibility: Possible but mitigated by adding firm-level equity return as a control and by restricting to first-time downgrades/LBO news.

A3. Syndicate size is predetermined relative to short-run CDS dynamics (i.e., lenders are in place long before a rating action).  
 Plausibility: DealScan shows loan facilities years earlier; not decided because of imminent downgrade.

A4. No spillovers: informed trading about Firm A does not systematically move Firm B’s CDS unless B shares fundamentals.  
 Plausibility: δt and industry fixed effects soak up common moves.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. Main Threats and Mitigations
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
T1. Anticipatory public information / rumour.  
 Fix: Control for daily equity returns; include media-coverage dummy; run robustness dropping events preceded by public 8-K or press releases.

T2. Omitted firm-specific shocks (e.g., earnings warning) unrelated to insider trading but correlated with syndicate size.  
 Fix: Include firm-specific time trends; perform firm-level placebo event studies using randomly drawn pseudo-event dates; compare high- vs low-lender difference under placebo.

T3. Selection bias: only firms with CDS quotes and DealScan data enter sample; these might differ systematically.  
 Fix: Show balance table; re-weight observations by propensity to have observable CDS; run inverse-probability weighting as robustness.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
```r
# Load libraries
library(data.table)     # fast manipulations
library(fixest)         # high-dimensional FE
library(lubridate)

#-----------------------
# 1. Load Data
#-----------------------
cds   <- fread("cds_quotes.csv")        # columns: entity_id, date, mid_quote
events<- fread("credit_events.csv")     # entity_id, event_date, event_type
loans <- fread("dealscan_syndicate.csv")# entity_id, loan_start, num_lenders
equity<- fread("equity_returns.csv")    # entity_id, date, ret
macro <- fread("controls.csv")          # date, vix, ind_cds

#-----------------------
# 2. Merge & Construct
#-----------------------
# Create daily panel of CDS quotes
setkey(cds, entity_id, date)

# Add equity return and macro controls
cds <- merge(cds, equity, by = c("entity_id","date"), all.x=TRUE)
cds <- merge(cds, macro,  by = "date",              all.x=TRUE)

# Add syndicate size (latest available before start of sample)
loans <- loans[ , .SD[loan_start == max(loan_start)], by = entity_id]
cds   <- merge(cds, loans[,.(entity_id, num_lenders)], by="entity_id", all.x=TRUE)

# HighLenders dummy
cds[, high := as.integer(num_lenders >= median(num_lenders, na.rm=TRUE))]

#-----------------------
# 3. Event-time mapping
#-----------------------
events[, event_date := as.Date(event_date)]
cds[, date := as.Date(date)]

cds <- merge(cds, events, by = "entity_id", all.x=TRUE, allow.cartesian=TRUE)

# Compute event time (days)
cds[, rel_day := as.integer(date - event_date)]

# Keep window ±60 days around events
cds <- cds[abs(rel_day) <= 60]

# Lead/lag dummies
lead_breaks <- c(-30,-20,-10,-5,-1,1,5,10,20,30)   # customise
for(i in 1:(length(lead_breaks)-1)){
    low  <- lead_breaks[i]; high <- lead_breaks[i+1]-1
    nm   <- paste0("lead",low,"_",high)
    cds[, (nm) := as.integer(rel_day>=low & rel_day<=high)]
}

# Outcome: daily log change in CDS spread
setorder(cds, entity_id, date)
cds[, log_cds := log(mid_quote)]
cds[, dlog_cds := log_cds - shift(log_cds,1), by = entity_id]

#-----------------------
# 4. Main Regression
#-----------------------
# build formula with all lead dummies except distant past (< -30) as base
lead_vars <- grep("^lead", names(cds), value=TRUE)
int_terms <- paste0(lead_vars,":high", collapse=" + ")
rhs       <- paste(c(lead_vars, int_terms,
                     "ret", "vix", "ind_cds"), collapse=" + ")

fml <- as.formula(paste("dlog_cds ~", rhs, "| entity_id + date"))

est <- feols(fml, data = cds, cluster = ~entity_id)
summary(est)

#-----------------------
# 5. Robustness: placebo events  (random event dates)
#-----------------------
set.seed(123)
placebo <- cds[, .(rand_date = sample(date,1)), by = entity_id]
cds_pb  <- merge(cds, placebo, by="entity_id")
cds_pb[, rel_pb := as.integer(date - rand_date)]
cds_pb <- cds_pb[abs(rel_pb)<=60]

cds_pb[, placebo_lead := as.integer(rel_pb>=-5 & rel_pb<=-1)]
est_pb <- feols(dlog_cds ~ placebo_lead*high + ret + vix + ind_cds |
                  entity_id + date, data=cds_pb, cluster = ~entity_id)
summary(est_pb)
```

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
If insider trading exists, βτ should be significantly positive for the last week (−5 to −1 days) and perhaps earlier (−10 to −6).  Magnitude: average CDS mid-quote ~200 bps; pre-event jump could be 5-10 bps (≈3–5% of level) within the final week.  γτ (interaction) should be additional 3-5 bps for high-lender firms, implying roughly double the abnormal move relative to low-lender entities.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist (Self-Assessment, 1 = satisfied, 0 = questionable)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
• Clear counterfactual / parallel trends      0.8  
• No simultaneity / reverse causality         0.7  
• Measurement accuracy of key vars            0.9  
• Robustness / falsification shown            0.8  
• External validity to broader CDS universe   0.6  

Overall, the proposed strategy should yield credible evidence on informed trading in CDS around credit events, with special attention to lender-based information channels.
